stories.article_text_excerpt: Figure caption, Watch: Ukraine's post office innovation helps isolated communities By James Landale Reporting from Zaporizhzhia oblast Published 15 September 2026 Every morning Igor Smelyansky looks at a vast map of Ukraine on his office wall and decides where he should put his people in harm's way. His aides provide him with live intelligence about Russian attacks and he deploys his teams, balancing their potential operational success against risk to life or limb. But Smelyansky is no military commander. He is the head of Ukraine's state postal service, Ukrposhta. And every day he must decide how far to send his postmen and women into the deadly "kill zone" along the front lines where the threat of drone attack is ever present. "If it's too dangerous to go today, we won't go," Smelyansky told us. "We'll go tomorrow, or we'll go somewhere else. The key is to be as agile as you can." Ukrposhta does more than just collect letters and parcels. It pays out pensions in hard cash, it takes payment for utility bills. We need heavy machinery to clear the rock and soil."Heavy machinery is often not readily available at small-scale mining sites. Sudan’s gold industry has become increasingly important since the civil war began in April 2023, providing a significant source of revenue in an economy devastated by conflict.The civil war began in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. As a result, the country is facing the world’s largest displacement crisis, with nearly 20 million people experiencing crisis-level hunger.

stories.title: EU moves closer to social media ban for under 13s
stories.summary: Ursula von der Leyen announces draft law to stop apps ‘depriving children of their childhood’ The EU will move forward with plans for an under 13s social media ban , the head of the European Commission has confirmed. Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday that social media apps were “depriving children of their childhood” and big tech platforms needed to prove the safety of their products. Continue reading...

stories.title: How extreme weather is hurting the global economy
stories.summary: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

stories.title: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack
stories.summary: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.

stories.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
stories.summary: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

stories.title: Congo's Ebola epidemic may have gone undetected for months
stories.summary: The deadliest Ebola outbreak on record in the Democratic Republic of Congo may have begun months before it was first declared in May.

stories.title: Iran: Activists sound alarm as regime seizes Baha'i assets
stories.summary: Rights groups warn Iran is increasingly confiscating assets from government critics and members of the country's Baha'i faith, but also actors, athletes and journalists living abroad.

stories.title: How the Houthis are also putting Egypt under pressure
stories.summary: The Houthis, a Yemeni rebel group, are expanding their control of maritime corridors in the Red Sea area. Their target is their avowed enemy Saudi Arabia. But the military moves also endanger Egypt.

stories.title: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?
stories.summary: Following Manuel Neuer's retirement, there are many candidates to succeed him, but which goalkeeper will Jürgen Klopp choose? What factors will play a role? And will Neuer's future have an indirect influence?

stories.title: Maduro ally Alex Saab pleads guilty to money laundering in US court
stories.summary: As part of the plea agreement, Saab agreed to cooperate with ongoing federal investigations in the United States and to hand over 195 million dollars (some €168.9 million) derived from the corruption scheme.

stories.title: Billions risk being locked out of the AI revolution due to smartphone costs
stories.summary: A new GSMA report finds that 3.4 billion people remain offline despite living within mobile broadband coverage, as rising component costs push smartphones further out of reach for the world's poorest.

stories.title: Surge in Yemen violence ends ceasefire and drives mass displacement
stories.summary: Thousands of Yemenis are fleeing renewed fighting and arriving at makeshift Al Kadha camp in Taiz. The UN says 125,000 people have been displaced in the past two weeks.

stories.title: Iran war has cost the US more than $38 billion so far, says Congressional Budget Office
stories.summary: The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office reports that up to $3 billion more is being spent on the war each month, depending on the intensity of fighting.

stories.title: From nail hammering to drilling, Japan’s new robots push physical AI forward
stories.summary: Technology companies gathered in Tokyo on 16 September 2026 for a one-day summit focused on physical AI, showcasing robots designed to perform tasks in the real world.

stories.title: Tall athletes can't stretch their legs in container beds at Asian Games, official says
stories.summary: South Korea's delegation slams the wooden containers housing its athletes at the Asian Games in Nagoya city.

stories.title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms
stories.summary: Sam Altman and other tech CEOs say there are incentives to limit advancements in AI, as fears grow over the threats it poses to humanity.

stories.title: Colombia and Brazil deadliest countries for environmental activists, report says
stories.summary: The two countries accounted for 52% of killings of environmental activists in 2025, according to Global Witness.

stories.title: Carney's new love-in with EU has everything to do with Trump
stories.summary: The Canadian PM is in Strasbourg this week seeking a "unique alliance" - and there is one clear catalyst.

stories.title: EU needs Georgia, foreign minister tells Euronews, reigniting enlargement question
stories.summary: Georgia’s top diplomat told Euronews that Tbilisi remains committed to EU accession and that Europe needs Georgia for its prosperity and security. But according to the FM, it all comes down to whether Europeans “are serious about enlargement”.

stories.title: Philippines' Duterte seen in person at International Criminal Court for first time
stories.summary: He is due to be tried for crimes against humanity over thousands of deaths linked to his war on drugs.

stories.title: Legendary Nigerian actor Olu Jacobs dies aged 84
stories.summary: Olu Jacobs was one of Nigeria's most recognised actors, whose career spanned several decades.

stories.title: Huge wildfire in Valencia region burns 690 hectares after Spain’s hottest summer
stories.summary: Spain’s firefighters were battling a major wildfire in Tuéjar, in the Valencia region, on 15 September, after flames spread through the Alto Turia Biosphere Reserve.

stories.title: US limits visas for South African officials over alleged anti-white discrimination
stories.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says South Africa has not addressed US concerns over racial inequality.

stories.title: Sniffing out trouble: Customs dogs remain vital in the age of AI
stories.summary: From synthetic drugs to concealed cargo, trained dogs can detect what scanners may miss. At a WCO forum in Tashkent, experts showed how canine units and new technology are increasingly working side by side.

stories.summary: Germany's chancellor nixxed his trip over doubts about his leadership after party losses to the AfD in state elections. Meanwhile, Defense Minister Pistorius is in Washington for talks with his US counterpart.

stories.title: Socialist Left leads far-right AfD ahead of Berlin vote
stories.summary: The results of the Berlin election are as hard to predict as ever. Three parties are vying for first place, including the socialist Left Party and the far-right AfD. But one issue is most important to Berliners.

stories.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
stories.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.
